About Helius

Helius is building the core infrastructure for Solana - empowering developers to create the next generation of crypto-powered applications. Our mission is to accelerate the development of internet capital markets by making it easier, faster, and more intuitive to build on-chain.

 

Thousands of teams - from early-stage startups to industry leaders like Coinbase, Phantom, and Jupiter - rely on Helius APIs, webhooks, and indexing tools to power their products. Backed by Haun Ventures, Founders Fund, and Foundation Capital, we’re a small, senior team obsessed with performance, simplicity, and scalability in decentralized systems.

 

Read our Helius Manifesto to see how we work and what we value.


About the Role

Helius runs its global edge network and high-performance services directly on bare metal. It's a deliberate choice for performance and cost, and it means the machines, the network, and the tooling that ties them together are ours to get right. This role joins our Platform team to make that fleet faster to provision, safer to access, cheaper to run, and boring to deploy to.

 

You'll work across the foundation everything else at Helius depends on: automating how servers get spun up and configured, standardizing how software gets built and shipped to machines, and executing on our engineering security roadmap. This is an intermediate role with a lot of room to grow. We care more about ownership, intensity, and learning speed than about a perfect match on today's stack.

 

No crypto background is needed. If you've run serious infrastructure anywhere, we'll teach you the blockchain parts.

 

What You'll Do

  • Automate the server lifecycle end to end: provisioning, OS installs, configuration, hardware validation, and decommissioning

  • Build and maintain the tooling engineers use to interact with the fleet, so nobody hand-configures a machine twice

  • Standardize how we build and deploy software to machines: CI pipelines, artifacts, deploy tooling, and rollbacks

  • Execute security roadmap items alongside our security lead: SSO-integrated access, jump hosts, secrets management, least-privilege access, and audit trails

  • Run cost analysis across the fleet, including cost per workload, provider comparisons, and hardware refresh decisions, and turn it into recommendations

  • Improve observability for the infrastructure you own, and take part in on-call and incident response

  • Write clear runbooks and docs so the rest of a remote team can operate what you build

 

What We're Looking For

  • Extreme ownership: you treat the systems you touch as yours, see problems through to the fix, and automate yourself out of repetitive work rather than living with it. You work the way our Manifesto describes (fast, direct, low-ego, and accountable), and that matters to us more than any single item below.

  • 3+ years in infrastructure, DevOps, SRE, or platform engineering

  • Hands-on bare metal experience, such as provisioning and managing physical servers (PXE, IPMI/BMC, RAID, NICs), working with colo or dedicated-server providers, and debugging hardware versus software issues

  • Deep Linux fundamentals, including systemd, networking, storage, and performance tuning

  • Experience with configuration management and infrastructure-as-code (e.g. Ansible, Terraform, Salt, Nix)

  • Solid scripting or programming ability in Python, Go, Bash, or similar

  • A security mindset: you think about access, blast radius, and secrets by default, not as an afterthought


Nice to Have

  • Rust experience, or interest in reading and debugging Rust services

  • High-performance networking or low-latency systems experience

  • Familiarity with ClickHouse, Prometheus, or Grafana

  • Experience at a high-scale B2B infrastructure company

 

Why Helius?

  • High-impact work: Your code will power applications used by millions across the Solana ecosystem, including Coinbase, Jupiter, and Phantom

  • Serious engineering: Build fast, reliable systems across distributed infra and high-throughput backends

  • Ownership & growth: Lead critical initiatives, influence architecture and product direction, and take on more responsibility as the company scales

  • Remote-first flexibility: Work where you’re most effective with a flexible, fully distributed team

  • Competitive comp & perks: Market-leading salary, meaningful equity, generous vacation, wellness budgets, and support for learning and travel

  • Mission-driven team: Join ambitious builders who move fast, take ownership, and are building infrastructure for internet capital markets

Join us in building the future of finance.

Our mission is to democratize finance for all. An estimated $124 trillion of assets will be inherited by younger generations in the next two decades. The largest transfer of wealth in human history. If you’re ready to be at the epicenter of this historic cultural and financial shift, keep reading.

About the team + role 

Robinhood’s Credit Card & Banking Product Engineering team conceptualizes, designs and builds our entire customer-facing product: from mobile application to underlying backend systems. Team members are trusted with full ownership over our innovative features and drive them from design to launch.

As a Senior Full Stack Engineer on Credit Card & Banking, you'll be expected to operate with outsized ownership and impact, leading high-leverage projects across our mobile app, backend services, and financial partner integrations. You'll partner closely with product, design, and peer engineering teams to strengthen the systems and technical foundations that let our product scale to millions of customers. The right candidate is a force multiplier: someone who drives ambiguous initiatives, shapes architecture across the stack, and raises the bar on execution for the whole team.

What you’ll do

  • Own the technical direction for major parts of Robinhood's Credit Card & Banking product, from mobile app to backend services, and drive them from early design through launch and iteration.
  • Lead the design of scalable, reliable systems that serve millions of users and integrate with world-class financial partners.
  • Break down ambiguous, cross-functional problems into clear technical plans, and align engineers, Product, and Design around them.
  • Set the bar for engineering quality through design reviews, code reviews, and best practices in reliability, security, and performance.
  • Mentor and grow the engineers around you, and raise the technical level of the whole team.
  • Partner with Product and Design to shape the roadmap, bringing an engineering view on tradeoffs, sequencing, and long-term architecture.

In addition to the base pay range listed below, this role is also eligible for bonus opportunities + equity + benefits.

Baton Corporation is the development company that builds and operates the entire technology stack behind pump.fun, the largest memecoin launchpad in production today. The systems are low latency, high throughput, live under constant load, and break if you get them wrong.

descriptions.job-11ks5el:
Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone’s reach while doing the most important work of your career.

What You’ll Do

As technology evolves, so do our tax reporting requirements, especially with the multitude of state and local taxes around the US.  Our state-related indirect obligations and filing requirements continue to grow with the business, and we are looking for someone who can not only maintain but help further build our US sales tax practice in achieving our tax goals.  This individual will need to be versed in indirect tax systems used in compliance, and be able to work with our talented group of engineers who support the state tax function. This position will report to the State & Local Tax Lead. 

This position can be office-based in Seattle, South San Francisco, Chicago, New York City, or Remote-US. 

Responsibilities

  • Help establish the direction, goals, and priorities for Stripe’s US indirect tax function, with a strong moral compass and integrity.
  • Manage and improve state indirect tax compliance systems across our portfolio of companies, and work with the tax reporting and eng teams to ensure coverage on all of our tax filings.  This includes systems used in compliance filings, business registrations, and working with our both tax and non-tax vendors to ensure we are meeting our compliance obligations.
  • Oversee and run point on special projects impacting US indirect tax systems. 
  • Run models and analyses for state indirect tax planning.  
  • Assist in data collection used in state controversy across different tax types and resolve tax issues.  
  • Monitor SALT developments across the US, including local impacts of federal law. 
  • Proactively identify areas for operational improvements and implement solutions to streamline downstream US indirect tax reporting.
  • Participate in special projects as needed including state tax attribute studies, nexus reviews, and evaluating state tax impacts of new tax regimes, M&A transactions, and new products before they launch.  

Who You Are

We’re looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

Minimum Requirements

  • 6+ years of relevant indirect tax experience, including in public accounting (Big 4 preferred) and/or - preferably - at a multinational publicly listed company.
  • Deep knowledge of state indirect tax issues and solutions in the technology industry.
  • A strong background in tax compliance, specifically US indirect taxes.
  • Experience in working with teams and engineers in building out US indirect tax infrastructure.
  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with a proven ability to research and communicate complex technical tax issues clearly to non-tax team members and work effectively across functional teams.
  • Flexibility to react quickly to changes in state tax laws including proposed changes as well as changes in the company’s products and services.
  • Exhibit strong analytical thinking, ability to work in a fast-paced environment with excellent prioritization and organizational skills.
  • Empathy, humility, and some comedy

You will also likely have (not required):

  • An advanced degree or professional qualification in tax, accounting, or law (CPA, JD or Master’s degree).
  • Experience working in a high-growth, rapidly scaling environment.
  • Industry experience at a multinational organization; experience working in technology, payments, or financial services is a plus.
  • A willingness to work with a diverse crew of tax nerds who care deeply about Stripe’s tax issues and each other.

The Firm:     


Brevan Howard Investment Management is one of the leading absolute return/hedge fund managers, overseeing assets on behalf of institutional investors from around the world, including pension funds, endowments, insurance companies, government agencies, private banks, and fund of funds.

Brevan Howard was founded in 2002 and launched its flagship global macro strategy in April 2003. The firm currently manages over $34bn and engages predominantly in discretionary directional and relative value trading in fixed income, FX markets, and equities. BH Digital, a division within Brevan Howard that manages crypto and digital asset strategies was launched in 2022.

The firm currently employs over 1,000 personnel worldwide, including over 400 investment professionals. This global presence gives Brevan Howard the ability to identify and source attractive investment opportunities, as well as investment management talent wherever they may be. Brevan Howard has won several industry awards for excellence in risk management, operational robustness, and investment performance.

The firm’s main hubs are in London, Jersey, Geneva, New York, Austin, Hong Kong, Singapore, Abu Dhabi and Bengaluru.

Info about the team

 

The Shared Services Hub is a cross-functional initiative aimed at creating collaboration across the Brevan Howard back office, bringing together Finance, FP&A, Procurement, Accounts Payable, Payroll, Tax and Legal. The Hub is based in Bengaluru and supports colleagues across Brevan Howard’s global offices.

These roles report into the Enterprise Systems & Operations team, which owns the platforms and automation underpinning the end-to-end process, but you will spend most of your time working directly with the various departments on a rotational basis. For example, you might support Finance during month-end, Procurement during negotiations and Legal vendor management. Rotations are designed to give you full training and knowledge across the entire back-office process.

This is a great opportunity for an entry-level candidate to learn how the back office of a hedge fund operates and to understand all of its areas, with exposure across the business from day one. You will also receive regular hands-on support and mentoring from the Enterprise Systems & Operations leadership, who will visit Bengaluru regularly, as well as a named point of contact based in Bengaluru for each rotation.

We are looking for two proactive, adaptable and ambitious candidates to join the Hub in Bengaluru as Shared Services Analysts. The ideal candidate brings natural problem-solving ability, strong attention to detail and a real appetite to learn. Full training is provided.

MAIN DUTIES/RESPONSIBILITIES OF THE ROLE: 


Essential Responsibilities:

What you will do across the Hub

  • Rotate through the supported departments, working directly with each team and learning their processes end to end.
  • Help manage BAU activity across our finance and operations platforms, following documented processes and standards.
  • Provide flexible capacity where demand is highest, covering peaks, absences and new workloads.
  • Take part in structured training and cross-training to build working knowledge of the entire back-office process.
  • Build strong working relationships with colleagues and stakeholders in each department and across regions.
  • Flag errors, exceptions and risks early to the relevant department and to your manager.
  • Help document and improve processes, looking for opportunities to streamline and automate manual work, particularly via the use of AI tools.

 

Examples of what you could support and learn:

Procurement

  • Administering supplier contracts in Workday and supporting routine procurement projects.

Payroll

  • Supporting payroll integration reviews, monthly closures and routine audits.

Legal

  • Legal management and supplier onboarding support into the legal vendor and payment management system, BrightFlag.
  • New fund and company creation.

Accounts Payable & Finance Operations

  • Creating and adjusting supplier invoices in Zip, including tax treatment and approvals.
  • Executing settlement runs and cost allocation runs, and updating payment acknowledgement statuses.
  • Supporting bank reconciliations, prepaid amortisation schedules and system alerts.
  • Creating supplier master records and updating remit-to details where automated feeds are unavailable.
  • Supporting month-end close, including journal matching, reconciliations, adjustments and ledger period status updates.

FP&A

  • Supporting forecast bridging, forecast-versus-actuals reviews and variance analysis.
  • Preparing reporting packs and providing UAT support ahead of go-lives.

WORK EXPERIENCE/BACKGROUND:


ESSENTIAL


  • A strong graduate, or someone with early experience in finance operations or shared services — we are more interested in aptitude and potential than years of experience.
  • Willingness to learn quickly and move between teams and tasks as priorities change.

descriptions.job-0eje5p9:
About Arca

Arca is a wealth management firm built from the ground up with AI. Most people get financial advice that's reactive: an annual check-in, a plan that's a document instead of a living thing, a relationship where you're one of three hundred clients your advisor is trying to remember. We think that's backwards. The kind of service that used to require a team of specialists behind you, the kind that makes you feel like the only person in the room, should be available to far more than the ultra-wealthy.

So we're building it. We're not SaaS — we are the wealth management business, rebuilding it from the inside with AI. Our platform is an Iron Man suit for advisors: it takes over the low-leverage work so they can focus on what actually requires a human, showing up with empathy, context, and judgment. Underneath, it keeps a living understanding of each client. It remembers the thing you mentioned once, six months ago. It notices when your life changes — a new job, a new kid, a market shift — and adjusts before you think to ask. You won't see the technology. You'll just notice your advisor seems to know you better than any financial professional ever has.

That's the product we're growing: client by client, on the strength of the experience itself. We started by acquiring firms managing over $1B in client assets, which gave us real advisors, real clients, and real financial outcomes to build against from day one. But acquisition was the starting line. The bet is that an advisor backed by this platform delivers something good enough that clients come to us on their own.

It's a $20T market, and we think it's ready to be rebuilt.
— Rron, CEO

The receipts

  • Stage: Series A, $64M raised

  • Backed by: General Catalyst, Index Ventures, Venrock

  • Board & Advisors: Former CEO of Vanguard, Former CFO of Schwab, Founder of Altruist, Morgan Housel (author of The Psychology of Money)

The team

We’re small on purpose and engineering heavy: about 80% of the team is technical. We’re based in NYC and hail from high growth startups like Stripe, Ramp, Rippling, Plaid, Doordash, & Glean.

We’re fully in-office in Flatiron, five days a week—lunch together, coffee breaks, basketball games, happy hours.

The role

As a Member of Technical Staff focused on TechOps, you'll own the IT foundation of a firm that is growing aggressively through acquisition. Roughly once a month through 2027, a new advisory firm somewhere in the country will join Arca. It arrives with twenty years of email, a server closet, a phone system nobody fully understands, and clients who should notice nothing except that things got better. You make that happen: from diligence, to day one, to the moment the last legacy system goes dark.

At the same time, you'll define how a fast-growing, regulated firm stays safe: identity, devices, networks, training, and the partners who help us run it all. You'll be the first leader of our newly formed TechOps function, setting its direction, deciding who we hire, and choosing which managed service providers we trust to extend it across the country. If it touches a laptop, a login, a phone line, or a firewall, you own it.

What you’ll build (and own)

  • The acquisition integration playbook. IT diligence before we sign, a clean cutover on day one, and the full migration after. Built to run once a month, in parallel, in cities you may never have visited, with each integration faster and cleaner than the last.

  • Identity and access for the whole firm. SSO, MFA, automated provisioning and deprovisioning, password management, and device management across Mac and Windows. The control plane that decides who can touch what, from an advisor's first day to their last.

  • The security roadmap. Network security, endpoint protection, email security, backup and recovery, incident response, and security awareness training, sized for a firm that holds client money and answers to regulators.

  • Compliance-grade systems. Email, text, and call archiving, books-and-records retention, and client data protection, built hand in hand with our Compliance team so we're exam-ready at every firm, every day.

  • Our MSP network. The external IT partners who give us hands on the ground nationwide. You'll pick them, set the bar, hold them to it, and replace them when they miss it.

  • The TechOps team. You'll set its direction, write the hiring plan, and build the team that scales this program as the firm does.

Example problems you’d work on

These aren’t hypothetical; we’re actively working on versions of all of these.

  • Moving twenty years of history without losing a single email. A new firm runs on an on-prem Exchange server, a handful of personal Gmail accounts, and a shared drive with a decade of client documents. You'll move mail, calendars, contacts, and files into our tenant, cut over the domain and its MX records, keep every legal and regulatory retention intact, and have advisors working normally on Monday morning.

  • Consolidating Google and Microsoft tenants. Every firm arrives on Google Workspace, Microsoft 365, or a mix of both, with shared mailboxes, aliases clients have emailed for twenty years, and domains we can't afford to break. You'll decide what consolidates, what stays, and in which order, so that no client email ever bounces.

  • A day one that clients never notice. Phone numbers ported, the main line still rings, texts and calls archived, printers and scanners working, Wi-Fi secured, and every laptop enrolled in management. Coordinated with an MSP you just brought on, in an office you saw for the first time last week.

  • Identity as the control plane. A new hire starts Monday with a laptop configured and every app ready, with access scoped to their role. Someone leaves, and every login is gone in minutes. That has to hold across Mac and Windows, Google and Microsoft, 1Password, and dozens of SaaS tools, at a new firm every month.

  • A security baseline that scales with every acquisition. Each firm arrives with its own risk: shared passwords, a consumer router, unmanaged laptops, no MFA. You'll define the Arca baseline, measure every firm against it during diligence, and close the gaps on a schedule. Advisors are prime targets for phishing and wire fraud on client money, so the training program matters as much as the firewall.

  • Turning the runbook into software. We're an AI-native company. The repetitive parts of every integration—discovery inventories, migration checklists, account provisioning, MSP handoffs—are candidates for automation and agents. You'll work with our Platform engineers to make the twelfth acquisition dramatically easier than the first.

The kind of person who thrives here

You’re excited by ownership, ambiguity, and building things that matter.

  • You're fluent in both worlds. You've run deep in Google Workspace and Microsoft 365, and you're equally at home with Mac and Windows fleets. Tenant migrations, domain cutovers, MDM, networking, and phone systems are things you've done for real, more than once.

  • You lead and you stay hands-on. You can set a roadmap, hire a team, and hold an MSP to a high bar. You'll also get on a plane, walk into a server closet, and figure out what's actually plugged into what.

  • You're ambitious in a way specific to this work. You're protecting people's retirement savings and estate plans. A missed archive is a regulatory finding. An open firewall is a client's life savings at risk. That consequence makes you more careful, not slower.

  • You move fast, and you know speed and reliability aren't in tension here. A cutover weekend has no room for surprises. You plan for the failure modes, rehearse the rollback, and still hit the date.

  • You’re someone people actually want to be in the room with. For the advisors and staff at a newly acquired firm, you're often the first face of Arca, and you're changing every tool they use. You're patient, clear, and calm under pressure. Inside our small, tight-knit team in one office, five days a week, you're kind, direct, and low-ego, you can give candid feedback without being an asshole, and you’re genuinely energized by this environment (not just tolerant of it).

Why now is the moment to join

This is a narrow window with unusually high leverage.

  • We just came out of stealth, and we're growing fast. The team is intentionally small, the equity reflects that, and the ceiling is high. You'd be joining early enough that the work you do now directly shapes what the company becomes and what's possible next.

  • The acquisition engine is accelerating. We expect roughly one acquisition a month through 2027. Every integration you run teaches the next one, and the playbook you write becomes how Arca grows.

  • TechOps is a blank page. A brand-new team with no legacy and no template. You define the program, the stack, the partners, and the people.

  • The hard part is behind us, which means the interesting part is starting. The platform is live, the concept is proven, advisors have moved real client assets onto it. The work now is scaling a working firm across a new acquisition every month, safely.

ABOUT THE ROLE

The Mechanical Systems Expert is Managed Services' expert embedded in a data center build - supporting design review and commissioning to ensure cooling systems are operable and maintainable at turnover. Every design decision eventually becomes someone's 3 a.m. problem; this role reviews the design and witnesses the testing on behalf of that person.


Some of the key responsibilities you should expect are the following:

Operability Design Review

Review mechanical and cooling designs - chilled water plants, air and liquid cooling systems, CDUs, CRAHs, heat rejection, water treatment - through an operations lens: maintenance access and laydown, isolation and redundancy behavior, degraded-mode operation, instrumentation adequacy, and failure-mode consequences. File review comments that change designs, not just document concerns.

Construction-Phase Verification

Walk mechanical installations at key milestones: pipe routing and support, valve access, equipment clearances, insulation quality, and cleanliness/flushing protocol compliance - catching operability problems while they're still cheap to fix.

Commissioning Witness

Witness Level 3-5 commissioning of mechanical systems: functional performance tests, staging and failover sequences, failure scenarios, and integrated systems testing. Drive operational issues into the Cx log with clear acceptance criteria and verify closure personally.

Turnover Readiness

Verify mechanical turnover packages: O&Ms, as-builts, valve tags and system labeling, water treatment baselines, spare parts and consumables lists, and PM program inputs (frequencies, procedures, vendor contacts). Validate training actually equips operators to run the plant.

Operations Transition Support

Support early operations stabilization post-turnover: alarm tuning input, setpoint refinement, and first-months troubleshooting alongside the operations team.

Program Feedback

Feed operational lessons into Hut 8 mechanical design standards and the next project's basis of design.

ABOUT YOU

What we're looking for:

  • 8+ years in critical facilities mechanical operations, commissioning, or chief-engineer-track roles.
  • Deep hands-on knowledge of chilled water plants, hydronic systems, and data center cooling topologies - air-cooled, water-cooled, and liquid/direct-to-chip.
  • Level 1-5 commissioning fluency from the witness/operations side, including integrated systems testing.
  • Sharp eye for maintainability in design reviews: access, isolation, and instrumentation gaps.
  • Turnover documentation rigor - you read the O&M before signing for it.
  • Comfortable embedded with a construction team while holding the operations line.
  • Water treatment and cleanliness protocol experience for critical hydronic systems.
  • CFC/EPA certifications, trade licensure, or engineering degree all welcome paths.

ABOUT THE WORK ENVIRONMENT

  • Full time on-site in St. Francisville, LA.

You’ll build the brand, generate demand and support growth across B2B segments (SMEs, enterprises, payment partners) and B2C segments (remittance users), in several markets. You’ll lead a team, own the budget and work closely with Sales, Product, BD and Compliance to turn marketing into revenue.
We’re looking for a Head of Marketing to own the marketing strategy for our cross-border payments business. You’ll build the brand, generate demand and support growth across B2B segments (SMEs, enterprises, payment partners) and B2C segments (remittance users), in several markets. You’ll lead a team, own the budget and work closely with Sales, Product, BD and Compliance to turn marketing into revenue.

descriptions.job-18lal99:
Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies - from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups - use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About the team

The Product Operations team supports Stripe’s mission (to ‘Increase the GDP of the Internet’) by enabling efficient, user-centered product development at scale. We create, manage, and implement central programs across Stripe that optimize Product development and delivery.

The team drives critical, cross-functional initiatives and delivers strategic analyses, such as:

  • Defining launch processes and policy
  • Managing launch processes and execution within product orgs
  • Planning and alignment across Product, Go-to-Market, and Systems / Operations teams
  • Leading commercial execution for priority product launches
  • Aggregating user feedback

We are a team-oriented group that collaborates closely with each other and our cross-functional stakeholders. Together, we identify opportunities to design and scale repeatable processes, and we bring clarity and insight to address ambiguous and complex problems at the intersection of go-to-market and product. 

What you’ll do

Responsibilities

  • Lead end-to-end operational readiness and execution for priority product launches, establishing owners, milestones, decision forums, and launch plans.
  • Manage commercialization program to drive cross-functional coordination between product and cross-functional teams and transform it into a scalable program that keeps pace with launch velocity.
  • Continuously examine, experiment, and implement measured improvements to our operational model and processes (e.g. automating tasks, building agentic workflows, developing repeatable methodologies)
  • Build with a mindset of scale and flexibility for all internal and external stakeholders
  • Partner with Product teams to help them execute on important strategic initiatives or drive operational scale and efficiency
  • Build and communicate relevant operational metrics to leadership and partnering teams

Who you are

We're looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

Minimum requirements

  • 6+ years of experience in product operations, technical program management, project management, a product ownership role, management consulting or related discipline
  • Previously worked cross-functionally with product and technical teams
  • Must have proficiency with Google suite, especially Google Sheets and Google Slides
  • Experience with AI, automation, and workflow tools to drive operational efficiency
  • Problem solving and analysis experience (solving business problems - commercial, operational, financial) in a GTM org and/or Sales-oriented environment
  • A strong track record of delivering complex initiatives end-to-end with multiple stakeholders in a changing, ambiguous environment 
  • Enthusiastic “roll up your sleeves” mentality

Preferred qualifications

  • Prior experience with payments, fintech, and/or high-growth technology companies
  • Experience working with and translating SQL and working with dashboards
descriptions.job-1d5qrq5:
Founded to transform retail finance, Ajaib Group is an Indonesian fintech unicorn breaking barriers to financial access. Having recently secured a $270M Series C—the single largest funding round in Southeast Asia over the past four years—we are backed by premier global investors including Y Combinator, Ribbit Capital, SoftBank, and SBI Holdings.  

To build world-class products, we assemble world-class talent. Supported by our fully remote work arrangement, our team spans Eastern Europe, the Middle East, India, and Southeast Asia, allowing you to work with brilliant engineers and builders from around the globe from wherever you are. We operate with an impact-driven purpose where everyone is the owner of our customers' satisfaction. Driven by a growth mindset and a fierce will to win, we refuse to settle and constantly push engineering boundaries.

Role Overview

As a Sr. Backend Engineer II - TL in the US Stocks team, you are the technical lead of a squad that builds the backend for trading US stocks. You lead design, delivery and code quality for the squad, and you stay hands-on in the code. You are not a people manager: you guide the work and the engineers technically, while the Engineering Manager owns hiring and performance. You partner with Product, Operations, Compliance and our US brokerage partners to deliver features that are accurate and reliable.

  • Lead the technical design for your squad's features, write design documents and run design reviews.
  • Break down epics into clear tasks, give realistic estimates and keep delivery on track, unblocking engineers when needed.
  • Stay hands-on: build the most critical and complex parts of the system yourself.
  • Set and uphold code quality standards through code review, testing practices and coding guidelines.
  • Make correctness the first rule of the squad: accurate money and quantity handling, idempotent requests, safe retries and audit trails.
  • Lead integrations with US brokerage and custody partners, including reconciliation of our records with theirs.
  • Lead incident response and root cause analysis for your squad's services, and drive lasting fixes.
  • Manage technical debt openly and negotiate trade-offs with Product and the Engineering Manager.
  • Coach and mentor engineers in the squad and help them grow technically.
  • Work with the Engineering Manager, Staff Engineers and Architecture on technical direction across teams.
  • Design and implement Smart Order Routing (SOR) logic or multi-venue execution strategies to optimize fill rates and latency across different Liquidity Providers (LPs) and exchanges.
  • Define and enforce strict API contracts and WebSocket streaming standards between the backend trading engine and the frontend/mobile teams to ensure real-time UI responsiveness.
  • Education: Bachelor's degree in Computer Science or equivalent practical experience.
  • Experience: 6+ years of professional backend engineering, including 1+ year leading a squad or project technically.
  • Languages: Highly proficient in Java, Go or another modern backend language.
  • System Design: Strong in microservices, event-driven design, reliability and observability, with a record of writing and defending design documents.
  • Data & Messaging: Solid experience with relational databases (query tuning), Kafka and Redis.
  • Infrastructure: Experience running services on cloud platforms (GCP or AWS) with CI/CD.
  • Leadership: Able to plan and deliver work with a team, give clear technical direction and mentor engineers, without needing formal authority.
  • Mindset & Domain: Ownership mindset and clear communication. Experience in brokerage, trading, payments, cross-border money movement or another regulated environment is a strong plus.
  • Direct experience integrating with modern API-first brokerage platforms (e.g., Alpaca, DriveWealth, Interactive Brokers) or crypto exchanges.
  • Performance Bonus - Get rewarded for the impact you make
  • Private Insurance - Comprehensive health coverage for you 
  • Paid Time Off - Take the time you need to recharge and come back stronger
  • Learning & Development - Company-sponsored training, courses, and professional certifications
  • Hybrid Work Arrangement - Enjoy the flexibility of working both remotely and from the office
  • Career Growth - Work closely with experienced leaders and take on meaningful ownership as we scale
  • Employee Perks - Enjoy exclusive discounts, partnerships, and lifestyle perks
  • Collaborative & High-Ownership Culture - Work with smart, driven people in cross-functional teams, take ownership, and make a meaningful impact for our users.

descriptions.job-1e22grh:
BitGo (NYSE: BTGO) is the digital asset infrastructure company delivering custody, wallets, staking, trading, financing, stablecoins, and settlement services from regulated cold storage. Since 2013, BitGo has focused on accelerating the transition of the financial system to a digital asset economy. BitGo maintains a global presence and multiple regulated entities, including BitGo Bank & Trust, National Association, the first federally chartered digital asset trust bank owned by a publicly traded company. Today, BitGo serves thousands of institutions, including many of the industry's top brands, financial institutions, exchanges, and platforms, and millions of investors worldwide. For more information, visit www.bitgo.com.

This role will require being full-time onsite at our Palo Alto office to support collaborative team dynamics and innovative problem-solving.

BitGo is looking for a design leader who still designs. You will manage and mentor the design team, own the design system, and sit next to the Chief Product Officer on business strategy.

This is a player-coach role, and we mean it literally. You will carry your own design surfaces and ship them, alongside leading the team. Expect roughly 50% hands-on IC work to start, decreasing as the team scales. It will not go to zero — the person setting the craft bar should be practicing at it.

We are not a design-forward company today. We intend to become one, and we want you to lead that shift.

The team you will lead

The design team is small, senior, and self-sufficient. Each designer owns a wide vertical outright — trading, staking, DeFi vaults, earn, wallets, financing — with deep product context and strong opinions about the work. They are running at capacity, which is part of why this role carries real IC load: you will pick up the retail mobile experience and design system rather than distributing that work across a team that is already full.

What they have asked for is specific, and we are hiring against it: a leader who gets into the work early with product and engineering rather than arriving at the end, who can critique craft because they still practice it, who tells them plainly what the next level requires, and who gives the team air cover so they can do the deep work instead of patching to hit dates.

What you will own

  • Your own design work. You will own surfaces directly and ship them at the quality bar you are asking of everyone else. Discovery through spec, in Figma, in the reviews, on the hard problems.
  • The team's growth. Invest in each designer individually. Be explicit about what the next level requires and give people the work that gets them there. Feedback should be candid, specific, and about the craft. Respect the ownership designers already have — autonomy is how this team works best, and your job is to raise the ceiling, not take the pen.
  • Design's standing in the company. Amplify the team's visibility, voice, and strategic impact. Represent design in strategy, roadmap, and architecture conversations, and push for the client experience when nobody else in the room will.
  • Upstream involvement. Join product and engineering at discovery, not at handoff. Shape long-term roadmaps with PMs so the team builds toward a direction instead of absorbing late changes.
  • The design system. Own the system and component library end to end: tokens, patterns, governance, contribution model, and adoption across product teams. Translate company strategy into a system flexible enough that teams ship scalable experiences rather than one-off patches.
  • Systems design. Our platform spans seven product areas with shared primitives — accounts, wallets, assets, entitlements, approvals. Design the system, not the screen.
  • The discipline. Establish UX and systems thinking as a practice the whole organization runs on, not a stage a design team owns. Product managers, engineers, and business leads should be able to frame a client problem, map the system it lives in, and evaluate a solution against real client needs. That is how we ship value to every client type we serve, in every market we operate in — rather than a set of features that work for the loudest account.
  • How we work. Establish the processes a small team needs to move fast without losing quality: critique, documentation, design review, and clean handoffs with engineering. Set the quality bar and hold it, including for AI-assisted work.
  • Technical depth. Read a technical design, understand the constraint, and decide with engineering where to compromise, where to hold, and where a broader change is worth the cost. Get into the mechanics with the team on the hard edge cases — the crypto ones and the design ones.
  • The face of design. Be present and known internally, and represent BitGo design externally with clients, partners, and candidates.

What success looks like

By six months: the design system has a clear owner, a versioned component library, and measurable adoption. Product teams stop reinventing patterns. You have shipped design work of your own that the team points to as the standard. Every designer knows what their next level requires and has work that supports getting there.

By 12 months: design is in the room early on strategy, not late on execution. Product and engineering partners frame problems in client terms without being asked. The team has grown in size and capability. At least one flagship surface has shipped with a coherent, systemized experience clients notice.

Who you are

  • Experience leading design in financial services. Digital assets, or another domain of genuinely complex technical flows, strongly preferred.
  • You have built and owned a design system at scale, not just used one.
  • Hands-on in Figma and a role model for craft. You are shipping design work today, not describing work you shipped four years ago. You can sit in a critique and give feedback that is specific enough to act on.
  • Deep in UX. Strong product thinking, logical reasoning, and decisions grounded in data rather than taste alone.
  • You have managed designers and made them better. You care about how the team is doing, not only what it ships.
  • Technically literate. Comfortable with APIs, data models, and engineering trade-offs.
  • Direct communicator. You can hold a position with a Chief Product Officer, an engineering lead, or a client, and change your mind when the argument is better.
  • You want the mandate. Turning a technical, compliance-heavy platform into a design-led one is the appeal, not the obstacle.

Helpful, not required

  • Regulated environments: broker-dealer, trust company, bank, or qualified custodian.
  • Experience with complex permissioning, approval workflows, or multi-entity account structures.
  • Design leadership at a company that went through the same shift you would lead here.

Why Join BitGo?

Disrupting an industry takes vision, innovation, passion, technical chops, drive to deliver, collaboration, and execution. Join a team of great people who strive for excellence and personify our corporate values of ownership, craftsmanship, and open communication. We are looking for new colleagues who bring innovative ways of thinking and problem-solving, and who want risks to be part of the team that changes the world’s financial markets.

  • Competitive base salary, bonus, and stock options
  • 100% company-paid health insurance for employee, partner, and dependents
  • Up to 4% 401k company match
  • Paid parental leave, Paid vacation
  • Free commuter/parking pass
  • Free custom lunches and snacks
  • Computer equipment and workplace furniture to suit your needs
  • Great colleagues and an inspiring environment

Benefits may vary based on location.

Pay Transparency Notice:

Depending upon your leveling and location, the compensation for this role averages between $210,000 and $250,000 USD base salary. Equity, an annual performance bonus, and the benefits outlined above are also part of this role’s package.

Cryptocurrencies are the most disruptive change the financial services industry has seen in years. Join us and you'll be able to look back and say you were part of the team that transformed investing.
descriptions.job-025ov31:
About the company
 
Hi, we're Ondo Finance. Our mission is to provide institutional-grade, blockchain-enabled investment products and services. We have both a technology arm that develops decentralized finance technology, and an asset management arm that creates and manages tokenized funds. We are the global leader in tokenized treasuries, tokenized stocks and ETFs, and are building the future of institutional-grade financial services onchain.
 
Founded by folks from Goldman Sachs Digital Assets Team, we’re backed by some of the best investors in the world including Founders Fund, Coinbase Ventures, Pantera Capital, Tiger Global, and more. We are currently the leaders in the space in terms of AUM and are well capitalized to continue growing the firm. We're fully remote, with team members across the U.S.
 
About the role

Ondo Finance is looking for a Senior Product Designer to own, hands-on, the design systems behind everything we ship. You'll own two outright, institutional and consumer, and support the marketing team's system so brand and design-to-code stay tight. Our products move real money, so precision and accessibility are the floor, not the ceiling: we want institutional and consumer users alike to feel the craft, which makes visual expression and motion core to the system. You'll join a small, senior team that runs on high ownership and low ego, and this is a building role: you'll be in Figma and alongside engineers every day, shipping the components and tokens yourself while setting the direction for the systems you own.

Target Outcomes
  • Both design systems, institutional and consumer, fully adopted across their web and mobile products, with measurable coverage (share of screens built from system components) rising quarter over quarter.
  • Figma libraries and the front-end component library in parity: tokens, variants, and states match one-to-one, with drift caught and resolved as part of normal release cadence.
  • Every system component meets WCAG AA, with accessibility criteria documented and verified before release, and the systems carry a visual and motion language that users notice and teams can reuse.
  • Product teams ship faster: fewer one-off components, shorter design-to-build cycles, and a clear contribution path that teams actually use.
  • Documentation and governance that scale beyond the design team: engineers, PMs, and AI agents can build correctly from the system without a designer in the loop.
Responsibilities
  • Own two design systems end to end, institutional and consumer: components, design tokens, theming, patterns, and the Figma libraries behind them, across web and mobile. Support the marketing team's design system as needed so brand practice stays consistent and design-to-code stays smooth.
  • Define the expressive layer of both systems: visual language, motion principles, and the interaction details that make institutional and consumer products feel considered and alive, not merely correct.
  • Design and ship the full stack of the system, from primitives and atoms through molecules and organisms to page templates, with polished interaction details and the visual hierarchy, typography, and layout rigor that trading and financial interfaces demand.
  • Partner closely with UI engineers so that tokens and components map cleanly to the production component library, and so Figma and code stay in sync.
  • Define how the system works on mobile: platform-appropriate interactions, responsive and adaptive behavior, and parity rules between web and native surfaces.
  • Hold the system to WCAG 2.2 AA: color contrast, focus and keyboard behavior, motion, and screen-reader semantics baked into components rather than bolted on.
  • Write clear, usable documentation (usage guidelines, do/don't examples, contribution guides) that designers, engineers, and AI agents can all work from.
  • Run governance across teams: contribution and review process, versioning and deprecation, adoption tracking, and the forums where product teams propose and resolve system changes.
  • Audit the system proactively to find gaps, inconsistencies, and drift across products, then prioritize and drive the fixes without waiting to be asked.
  • Use AI tooling as part of daily work: agents, markdown guideline files, and MCP integrations that connect the design system to design and engineering workflows.
Requirements
  • 6+ years in product design, including 3+ years focused on design systems.
  • Experience building and scaling a shared design system across multiple products and platforms, web and mobile, including mobile-specific design systems and interactions.
  • Strong UI craft: visual hierarchy, typography, layout, and polished interaction details, with a point of view on motion and visual expression and the taste to know when restraint is the right call.
  • Builds scalable components and design tokens, including theming (for example light/dark modes or multi-brand).
  • A strong understanding of how components and tokens translate into front-end libraries: how components are built, composed, and consumed in code (for example React, React Native, or Swift/Kotlin component libraries), and how tokens flow from Figma into code.
  • Advanced Figma skills: variables and modes, auto layout, component properties, and library management at scale.
  • A track record of working closely with engineers as a day-to-day partner, not a handoff.
  • Strong accessibility knowledge and experience shipping WCAG AA compliant components.
  • Writes clear documentation and has run governance across teams: contribution models, review processes, and adoption.
  • Fluency with AI tooling in a design or engineering workflow: using agents, writing markdown guideline files, and working with MCP integrations.
  • Experience with design-to-code tooling such as Code Connect, token pipelines, or Storybook.
  • A systems thinker with sharp attention to detail who sees both the pattern and the pixel.
  • A portfolio that showcases design systems work: components, tokens, documentation, and the reasoning behind the decisions.

Nice to Have

  • Experience with crypto, onchain or tokenized-asset products.
  • Experience in fintech, exchanges, or trading platforms. Design systems for trading surfaces have their own nuances: dense data tables, real-time state changes, numeric typography, and color semantics for gains, losses, and risk.
  • Familiarity with crypto and digital-asset products, or with tokenized assets and markets.
  • Experience setting up motion and interaction standards within a system.
  • Working proficiency in Mandarin Chinese.
What we offer
  • Competitive compensation including but not limited to salary, future token rights, and/or equity (according to your preferences) — We are well-funded and believe that great talent deserves great compensation.
  • Full benefits (medical, vision, and dental) and flexible vacation policy (PTO).
  • Remote-first team across many countries — You will be an early team member helping shape our vision, culture, and design practices.
  • A+ colleagues — Our team includes alumni from: Goldman Sachs, Blackrock, Two Sigma, Bridgewater, SpaceX, AWS, Meta, Google, McKinsey, Circle, Uniswap.
  • Best-in-class investors — We are proud to be backed by leading crypto experts and VCs, including Pantera Capital, Founders Fund and Coinbase Ventures.
descriptions.job-0mvwvj1:
Build a Safer World.

TRM Labs provides AI-powered intelligence solutions that help public and private sector agencies investigate and disrupt crime. TRM's platforms enable investigators to trace illicit activity, build cases, and construct operating pictures of threat networks. Leading agencies and businesses worldwide rely on TRM to make the world safer and more secure.

Our ability to identify, hire, and retain exceptional talent is foundational to our mission. The Talent team at TRM is made up of seasoned professionals who have experience hiring world-class Engineering, Data Science, GTM, and People teams for the most notable startups in Silicon Valley. As a Product Recruiter, you will help drive the R&D Org's ability to attract, engage, and hire top talent at TRM. Your success will be measured by the velocity and quality of TRM's talent acquisition.

The impact you'll have here

  • Build a high-velocity recruiting engine that efficiently identifies and recruits the best technical talent to TRM.

  • Manage the full recruiting lifecycle across a variety of Product roles and teams.

  • Create positive candidate experiences throughout every touchpoint.

  • Develop creative and impactful sourcing strategies that will help us find and hire a diverse and exceptional team.

  • Continuously improve our recruiting processes and increase the efficiency of our hiring.

What we're looking for

  • 5-7+ years of Product recruiting experience in high-growth US-headquartered tech startups

  • Proven experience in hiring hard-to-fill product roles, with expertise in using sourcing tools, conducting market research, and developing personalized outreach strategies.

  • Ability to analyze and interpret recruiting metrics, conversion rates, and market data, using these insights to refine strategies and provide actionable feedback to hiring managers.

  • Quickly familiarize oneself with new roles and requirements, showcasing flexibility, curiosity, and a high tolerance for change in a fast-paced, high-growth environment.

  • Exceptional communication skills to work effectively with hiring managers, provide regular updates, and manage expectations. Skilled at building trust and acting as a strategic partner in the hiring process.

  • Strong persistence and a results-oriented mindset to handle challenges, follow up on passive leads, and meet ambitious outreach targets.

Learn about TRM Speed in this position:

  • Within 72 hours of receiving a position, you schedule the intake meeting, open the position in the ATS, post the description, design the interview process, configure the interview plan.

  • Within week of opening a position, you have conducted 5-10 Recruiter Screens and have conducted the first sync with the Hiring Team for calibration.

  • Two weeks after the initial interviews, you analyze the data to identify what is and isn’t driving pass rates and conversions. You share your insights and recommendations with the hiring team to refine and optimize the search, and you continue to monitor and adjust the approach until the position is filled.

Our Onboarding Process:

  • Within your first 30 days, you’ll be fully onboarded, calibrated, and operating as the DRI for your positions.

  • Within your first 60 days, you’ll have your first sourced candidates reaching final rounds.

  • Within your first 90 days, you’ll have made 3-4 hires.

The following represents the expected range of compensation for this role:

  • Individual pay is determined by skills, qualifications, experience, and location. The compensation details listed in this posting reflect the US base salary only.

  • The estimated base salary range for this role is $130,000 - $170,000.

  • Additionally, this role may be eligible to participate in TRM’s equity plan.

  • Please note – we factor in the different costs for geographies outside the United States.

Application Instructions

If you’re interested in joining TRM, we encourage you to apply directly. Every application is reviewed by our Talent team.

Before applying, review the job description carefully and highlight the experience and impact that best demonstrate the required qualifications. Please also provide thoughtful and accurate answers to the application questions, as these will be used to evaluate your skills and qualifications for the role.

If you send your resume directly to someone at TRM, we can’t guarantee it will reach the appropriate hiring team. Applying directly is the best way to ensure your application will be considered.

Interviewing with TRM

Our process is designed to understand how you think, solve problems, and deliver impact, while allowing you to evaluate TRM. Most interview processes include a case study, an AI skills assessment, and a Leadership Principles interview.

  • Recruiter Intro: Qualifications, motivations, and alignment with the role.

  • Hiring Manager: Deep dive into your relevant experience, skills, and impact.

  • First Round: 1–2 interviews focused on the skills most critical to the role.

About the job

About HIFI

HIFI is a stablecoin infrastructure company building technology for the next-generation of financial products. We build tools for payments and tokenized money products across money movement, cards, and capital markets. Institutions and enterprises already use our platform and APIs to move billions of dollars in production environments around the world, and we are still early.

 

Founded in 2022, our organization is flat and our team is talent dense. We work in person at our office in Flatiron and are intentional about who we work with. We've raised $37 million from world-class investors, including a Series A led by Left Lane Capital.

 

About the Team

HIFI's compliance team is what makes it possible for banks, fintechs, and institutions to move money on stablecoin rails with confidence. The team owns the BSA/AML program, sanctions controls, and client onboarding that every partnership and every dollar of volume depends on. As stablecoin regulation takes shape this role helps HIFI scales from an early-stage startup into a long-term, category-defining platform, this team will set the standard for how compliance is built into institutional stablecoin infrastructure, as a core part of the product rather than an add-on.

 

The Head of Financial Crime Compliance owns that effort day to day. You'll run HIFI's BSA/AML and sanctions program across both fiat and on-chain flows, and you'll be the primary point of contact for banking partners, auditors, and examiners. This is a senior role with real ownership: you'll set policy, manage and grow the compliance team, and work directly with product and engineering to turn regulatory requirements into onboarding flows and monitoring rules.

 

Responsibilities

  • Own HIFI's BSA/AML and sanctions compliance program across fiat and stablecoin flows, including the annual risk assessment and independent testing.

  • Oversee KYC/KYB and enhanced due diligence for institutional clients, fintechs, and financial institutions, and make final calls on high-risk onboarding decisions.

  • Manage transaction monitoring and investigations, including alert quality, escalation standards, and final review and filing of SARs.

  • Run sanctions screening (OFAC and other applicable lists) on clients, counterparties, and blockchain wallet addresses, and set the standards for resolving potential matches.

  • Serve as the primary point of contact for banking partners, auditors, and examiners, and own responses to diligence requests and exam findings.

  • Write and maintain compliance policies and procedures, including stablecoin-specific requirements under the GENIUS Act, and brief leadership on regulatory changes that affect the business.

  • Partner with product and engineering to design onboarding flows, monitoring rules, and system controls, and evaluate and select compliance vendors and tooling.

  • Hire, manage, and develop the compliance team, and set the processes that let the function scale with transaction volume.

 

You might be a fit if

  • 7+ years of relevant experience in BSA/AML, financial crime compliance, payments compliance, fintech compliance, banking, crypto, or a related field.

  • Experience operating at a senior individual contributor or management level within a regulated financial services, payments, fintech, crypto, or banking environment.

  • Strong working knowledge of BSA/AML, KYC/KYB, customer due diligence, enhanced due diligence, OFAC sanctions, transaction monitoring, and suspicious activity escalation.

  • Strong understanding of payment flows, including ACH, wire, RTP, cross-border payments, virtual accounts, and other bank payment rails.

  • Strong familiarity with stablecoins, digital asset transactions, blockchain-based settlement, wallets, and crypto compliance risks.

  • Experience working with compliance platforms such as Sumsub, Persona, TRM Labs, Chainalysis, or similar systems.

  • Demonstrated experience improving or redesigning manual compliance processes through automation, workflow design, tooling, or operational controls.

  • Strong judgment and the ability to distinguish between regulatory requirements, partner requirements, internal policy, and risk-based business decisions.

  • Ability to communicate complex compliance issues clearly to technical, operational, commercial, and executive stakeholders.

  • Strong project management skills and the ability to drive remediation and implementation work across multiple teams.

  • Comfort operating in a fast-moving environment where products, regulations, counterparties, and risk profiles evolve quickly.

 

Why This Role Matters

Every institution that moves money on HIFI's rails is trusting that the compliance behind them is airtight. This is a chance to build that trust from the ground up at a stablecoin payments infrastructure company as it scales, and to help set the standard for how compliance should work.

 

Additional Requirement

Must be within a commutable distance from our office and able to work in person most days of the week.
